levels.title: Level 1: Workspace Setup & Navigation
levels.objective: Learn to interact with the file system using the Linux CLI, create a clean directory workspace, set up your global developer identity, and initialize an empty repository instance.

tasks.name: Current Work Directory
tasks.instruction: Before initializing a project, check exactly where you are standing inside the system directory tree. Print the current working path.
tasks.hint: Type 'pwd' (Print Working Directory) and hit Enter.
tasks.successMessage: Success! The system reports your active path is /home/seneca/projects.

tasks.name: Create Folder
tasks.instruction: Create a new directory called 'git-game'.
tasks.hint: Use the command 'mkdir' followed by a space and the folder name 'git-game'.
tasks.successMessage: Directory created! A gray directory block labeled [git-game] is now tracked.

tasks.name: Move into the Folder
tasks.instruction: Change your current location to the new 'git-game' directory.
tasks.hint: Use 'cd' (Change Directory) followed by your target folder name.
tasks.successMessage: Navigation complete. Notice your terminal shell prompt string has updated.

tasks.name: Configure User Name
tasks.instruction: Git requires an author identity for commits. Configure your global system user name to be 'My Name'.
tasks.hint: Use: git config --global user.name "My Name"
tasks.successMessage: Global identity metadata name saved to config parameters successfully.

tasks.name: Configure User Email
tasks.instruction: Complete your global identity setup by linking your email address to 'student@senecapolytechnic.ca'.
tasks.hint: Use: git config --global user.email "student@senecapolytechnic.ca"
tasks.successMessage: Global identity email updated. Commit execution capabilities unlocked.

tasks.name: Init Git Repo
tasks.instruction: Convert this plain folder into an active, local tracking Git version control repository.
tasks.hint: Run the core Git initialization command: 'git init'
tasks.successMessage: Initialized empty Git repository! Hidden tracking directory .git/ generated.

levels.title: Level 2: Tracking Changes & Local Commits
levels.objective: Master the operational bridge between the Working Directory, the Staging Area, and a permanent Commit Node. Learn to inspect lines of modification and review historical logs before saving.

tasks.name: Create File
tasks.instruction: Create a text file named 'index.html'.
tasks.hint: Use the system utilities command 'touch' followed by 'index.html'.
tasks.successMessage: File added! An untracked, red-colored file icon element now appears.

tasks.name: Check Repository Status
tasks.instruction: Check the active state of your repository to verify how Git sees your new file.
tasks.hint: Type 'git status' to run a structural workspace diagnostics check.
tasks.successMessage: Status pass executed. Shell logs output: 'Untracked files present: index.html'.

tasks.name: View File Differences
tasks.instruction: Before staging your changes, inspect the exact modifications made to the lines inside your file.
tasks.hint: Type 'git diff' to output active working line transformations.
tasks.successMessage:
Diff rendered. Green marker block added: '+

Hello Git

'.

tasks.name: Stage File
tasks.instruction: Move the 'index.html' file into the Staging Area to prepare it for your milestone checkpoint.
tasks.hint: Run 'git add' targeting your explicit filename.
tasks.successMessage: Staged! The index.html file token switches behavior flags from red to green.

tasks.name: Create Commit
tasks.instruction: Permanently commit your staged changes into the repository history with a message labeled 'initial setup'.
tasks.hint: Ensure you add the -m flag string key wrapped inside matching double quotes.
tasks.successMessage: Snapshot captured! Timeline tracking history initialized with node marker C1.

tasks.name: View Commit Log History
tasks.instruction: Review your repository's commit history logs to confirm your milestone is logged with its author and hash.
tasks.hint: Type 'git log' to call up your project repository historical index list.
tasks.successMessage: Log array generated, displaying author Aleksandra, timestamps, and hash mappings.

levels.title: Level 3: Advanced Branching & Conflict Interventions
levels.objective: Isolate experimental feature creation via independent branching trackers, explore modern context switching syntax, and systematically handle structural merge conflicts.

tasks.name: Create a Branch
tasks.instruction: Create a new feature branch named 'feature-ui'.
tasks.hint: Use 'git branch' followed by your specific target path name 'feature-ui'.
tasks.successMessage: Branch initialized. A virtual workspace pointer extends off the main tracking root.

tasks.name: Switch to the New Branch
tasks.instruction: Change your active context to work on the 'feature-ui' branch using the traditional checkout syntax.
tasks.hint: Use 'git checkout' to redirect system tracking parameters.
tasks.successMessage: Context switched. Prompt string brackets now track: (feature-ui).

tasks.name: Use Modern Switch Syntax
tasks.instruction: Switch back to the stable main development branch using the modern alternative command line keyword.
tasks.hint: Type 'git switch' directly followed by your target line keyword 'main'.
tasks.successMessage: Context switched safely. Active pointer references main once again.

tasks.name: Experience an Unexpected Merge Conflict
tasks.instruction: Attempt to merge the changes from 'feature-ui' directly into your active 'main' branch.
tasks.hint: Run the integration step using 'git merge' and target the feature label name.
tasks.successMessage: CONFLICT! Automatic merge failed. Files highlight code block interference areas in orange.

tasks.name: Emergency Merge Abort
tasks.instruction: You are not ready to manually sort this conflict line-by-line right now. Run the safety-net command to cancel the merge entirely and reset to your clean state.
tasks.hint: Append the double dash abort option parameter flag straight onto your merge keyword.
tasks.successMessage: Merge process canceled. Files reverted safely back to pristine pre-merge states.

levels.title: Level 4: Remote Repositories & Collaboration
levels.objective: Link a local repository to GitHub, download existing templates via cloning, and securely synchronize project timelines back and forth across remote host instances.

tasks.name: Clone a Remote Repository
tasks.instruction: Download a copy of an existing remote repository hosted at 'https://github.com/seneca/template.git' to initialize your workspace templates.
tasks.hint: Execute 'git clone' followed directly by the complete remote endpoint location string.
tasks.successMessage: Download complete! Workspace loaded with layout templates from the server architecture.

tasks.name: Link Local Project to a Remote URL
tasks.instruction: For your local 'git-game' project, add a remote server connection named 'origin' pointing to the address 'https://github.com/seneca/game.git'.
tasks.hint: Syntax pattern structure: git remote add <name> <url_string>
tasks.successMessage: Remote mapping registered! Cloud pipeline icon established under unique key name origin.

tasks.name: Push Local Milestones to the Cloud
tasks.instruction: Upload your local repository tracking history checkpoints from your local machine up to the remote cloud server's main branch.
tasks.hint: Type 'git push' then provide the host marker label 'origin' and branch 'main'.
tasks.successMessage: Local file blocks processed and safely uploaded to remote server infrastructure archives.

tasks.name: Fetch Server Changes
tasks.instruction: Download the newest branch tracking details and commits uploaded by your project partner to the server without merging them into your local working files yet.
tasks.hint: Execute a fetch checkpoint check targeting the shorthand string destination label 'origin'.
tasks.successMessage: Fetch complete. Remote pointers aligned locally without changing working directory states.

tasks.name: Pull Down and Integrate Updates
tasks.instruction: Fetch and automatically merge the newest modifications from the remote server's main branch straight into your active local workspace.
tasks.hint: Execute the pull combined tracking method: git pull <remote_label> <target_branch>
tasks.successMessage: Success! System workspace synchronized seamlessly with server baseline commits.
